## What it is

A single preview arrangement of every box and tray in this project, laid out
the way they'd sit together in a drawer: the three bag-dispenser boxes in a
row, big on the left down to small on the right, with the tweezer tray
sitting in front of the whole row, centered on it. It's a layout, not a part
to print as one piece — each box and the tray still print and stand on their
own.

Uses the plain (non-Gridfinity-footed) versions of the three boxes, since
those are what a naming quirk in the current tooling lets this layout
reference by name; the grid-foot versions would need renaming first to
drop the space-and-hyphen in their names.

## Design notes

`gap_between_boxes` is the breathing room left between each box in the row.
`gap_to_tray` is the breathing room between the tray and the row it sits in
front of. Both are plain sliders; there's no fit behind either number.

Every box keeps its own footprint and height exactly as built; this part
only moves them, it never resizes or reshapes any of them. The three boxes
are lined up so their fronts (where the bag opening is) sit flush along one
straight line, even though the boxes themselves are different depths.

## Don't

- Don't expect this to export as one printable piece in the usual sense:
  it's four separate solids placed next to each other, not one fused shape.
  Export or print each box and the tray on their own.
- Don't resize a box by changing anything here. Open that box's own part and
  adjust its sliders; this layout will pick up the new size automatically.
